newsitem.title: USA: Dow sets record-high close but tech sector wilts.
newsitem.headline: Dow sets record-high close but tech sector wilts.

text.p: The Dow industrials limped to a record-high close on Friday despite weakness in the technology sector after software company Computer Associates warned of a revenue shortfall.

"Computer Associates almost stopped the Santa Claus rally. Technology stocks are coming under some pressure, particularly the software issues," said A.C. Moore, senior investment strategist at Dunvegan Associates.
The Dow rose 14 to end at about 6561, topping the previous all-time high of 6547.79 set on November 25.
Among other technology shares, Motorola fell 1-1/2 to 61-3/4, Intel fell 1-1/4 to 135-3/8, Microsoft lost 1-1/4 to 84-1/4 and IBM was off 5/8 to 155-1/4.

The broader market was firmer, with gainers outpacing losers by a 15-to-8 margin. With NYSE volume of about 252 million shares, it was the quietest full session so far in 1996. That distinction had been held by Thursday's session, when 253.4 million shares changed hands.
Stocks received underlying support from stronger Treasury prices. The long bond rose 20/32 to yield 6.54 percent after an unexpected 1.6 percent drop in November orders of durable goods.
It was the first decline in orders for big-ticket items in three months and stood in contrast with a 0.1 percent rise expected by Wall Street.
In another economic report, jobless claims fell to 335,000 for the week ended December 21, compared with 346,000 expected by private economists.
As for stocks outside the technology sector, Jim Benning, a trader at BT Brokerage, said some interest rate-sensitive issues declined even though bond prices rose.
Wells Fargo lost 1-5/8 to 278-5/8, Citicorp fell 1/4 to 106-3/8 and Bankers Trust slipped 1/4 to 88.
